questions.q: What defines a factless fact table?
options: It has no measure columns at all; a measurement is achieved by counting rows instead
It has no dimension keys at all
It is a fact table that is never actually loaded with data
It stores only text data, never numbers
questions.explain: A factless fact table records events or conditions with dimension keys but no numeric measure column — you measure it by running COUNT(*), not SUM().

questions.q: In the f_ClassAttendance example, how do you answer "how many students attended Tuesday's lecture"?
options: Run COUNT(*) grouped by class and date, since the row's existence is the measurement
SUM the Quantity column
AVERAGE the AttendanceDate_Date_FK column
This question cannot be answered from a factless fact table
questions.explain: Because there is no measure column, counting rows is how a factless fact table is queried — each row's presence represents one attendance event.

questions.q: What is the key difference between an event factless fact table and a coverage factless fact table?
options: In an event table every row means something happened; in a coverage table a row means a condition existed, whether or not an event actually occurred
Coverage tables always contain a measure column, unlike event tables
Event tables can never have more than one dimension key
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: Attendance is an event table — a row means the event happened. A promotion-eligibility table is a coverage table — a row means the condition existed, independent of whether a sale followed.

questions.q: Why is a coverage factless fact table useful when compared against a transaction sales fact table?
options: It can reveal which eligible products or accounts did NOT generate a transaction, a question the transaction table alone can't answer because it has no row for things that didn't happen
It replaces the need for the transaction fact table entirely
It automatically fixes missing rows in the transaction fact table
Coverage tables cannot be compared to transaction tables under any circumstances
questions.explain: Comparing coverage rows to transaction rows surfaces the absence of an event — eligible-but-unsold products, or assigned-but-inactive accounts — which a transaction-only view can never show.

questions.q: Across all of Chapter 2, which trait distinguishes a factless fact table from the other three fact table types?
options: It's measured by counting the existence of rows rather than summing a numeric measure column
It is the only type that uses a Date dimension key
It is the only type that can have more than one dimension key
It is the only type that is ever updated instead of inserted
questions.explain: Transaction, periodic snapshot, and accumulating snapshot fact tables all carry at least one measure column to sum; a factless fact table's signal is the row itself.
